title: Make self.name writable in DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
Background: #2664 added a name property to dedicated workers, passed at construction time. #2783 made it `[Replaceable]` to resolve a [compatibility issue](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1375457).

The motivation for this change is to enable a [debugging story](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pvyZJOcKUuptgNVVgU9ZDkLgAJPm9e1pAhI8LRA9bS0/) for web apps built with Emscripten (or any web app that utilizes a web worker pool): disambiguating between workers whose purpose/name is only known post-construction.

Some more background on the Emscripten use case: Emscripten implements the pthread library for the web by using a web worker for each thread. Multiple workers may be created at start up and stored in a pool for later thread allocation (`-s PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE`), or they can be created just-in-time, but either way the pthread API separates thread creation from assigning a name (`pthread_setname_np`) so there is no way to assign an application-provided name for the web worker at construction time.

Today, `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope.name` is used in browser devtools to customize various UI surfaces (or if missing, the worker script url is used). In all browsers, if a worker sets `self.name` at runtime nothing changes in the devtools UI. Devtools may technically get this functionality working in a spec-compliant way (since this has been marked replaceable), but implementation-wise it would be be better if this property was writable.
